analysis:
The batch contains only documentation: changelog.d/serving-stalls.md (new) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (mermaid edits at lines 298-299 and a new paragraph at head lines ~361-395). I found no source code, wire protocol, attestation, key-handling, or authorization changes in the supplied evidence.

The documented behavior concerns the MLX buffer-cache sweep, retained free paged-KV segments, and load-gate release ordering. Retained segments are uncommitted, hold no ledger charge, and are dropped on a refused charge or memory pressure. Security-relevant points to check in the unseen implementation:
- A-001 / T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory): retained KV segments are reused across requests, possibly across consumers. The doc says new segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages, but it does not say whether a reinstalled retained segment is re-zeroed or overwritten before another request uses it. If a retained segment is reinstalled without zeroing, one request's KV data could be exposed to another request's attention reads. Attention masking normally prevents reads of unwritten slots, but that is unverified here. This is a doc-level concern only, since no code was supplied.
- T-010 / T-029 (DoS and resource monopolisation): the 5 s whole-Mac idle gate, the 30 s retention timeout, and the memory-accounting change are availability/accounting behaviors. Retained segments are not counted in the ledger, yet they are allocator-active memory. Consumers who control request timing could influence reclaim behavior, though the doc says refused charges drop retention.
- T-041: the prefix cache is unchanged; this PR only touches the in-memory KV pool.

No claims in the docs weaken documented controls. No concrete regression is demonstrable from documentation alone. Integration should verify in provider-swift (CBv2RetainedKVSegments, KVPoolReclaimer, GlobalKVCacheBudget.directChargeRefusalSignal) that reinstalled segments are cleared or never readable outside written positions, and that the reclaim paths cannot be driven by a consumer into repeated flushes. That code is not in this batch, so I set needs_deeper_review=true.
